ai.description: This 15–18 cm salamander is dark brown to black with bright orange markings on the head, spine, and tail. It features prominent, rib-bearing dorsal warts and a distinct, bony cranial ridge.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Tylototriton himalayanus* is best distinguished by its prominent, orange-to-yellowish vertebral ridge and distinct, rib-bearing glandular warts along its flanks.
ai.habitat: The Himalayan salamander inhabits moist, subtropical broadleaf forests and agricultural ponds at elevations ranging from 1,200 to 2,500 meters in the Eastern Himalayas.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan salamander is primarily nocturnal, emerging from forest leaf litter during rainy nights to forage for small invertebrates like earthworms and insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Tylototriton himalayanus* reproduces via aquatic egg-laying, typically depositing 100–200 eggs in ponds or pools during the monsoon season (June to August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Tylototriton himalayanus* occurs in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically within the Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh and West Bengal, at elevations of 1,500–2,500m.
ai.callDescription: The Himalayan salamander (*Tylototriton himalayanus*) is silent, as it lacks vocal cords and does not produce an advertisement call in its high-altitude forest habitat.
